title: Warranty claims on the Torrent 9 dishwasher: three sources
bodyMd:
**Source 1 — Memo from the Service Director, 6 May**

Warranty claims on our Torrent 9 dishwasher have risen sharply since January. Of the 1,240 claims logged from January to April, 812 cite the drain pump. We changed drain-pump supplier from Velmark to Ostrey for every unit built on or after 1 December; every Torrent 9 built before that date carries a Velmark pump. Units reach the customer on average two weeks after they are built, and the warranty runs for two years from that date. The Ostrey pump is the only component we have changed supplier on. I propose we revert to Velmark for all production from 1 July.

**Source 2 — Email from the Supplier Quality Manager, 11 May**

Two cautions before we revert. First, the Ostrey pump is not the only thing that changed on 1 December: the same engineering release narrowed the drain hose from a 22 mm to a 19 mm internal bore so that it would fit the revised cabinet, and a narrower bore raises the pressure the pump must work against. Second, our claim records classify a fault as "drain pump" whenever the machine fails to clear the sump, which a blocked or kinked hose will also cause; the component itself is inspected only on the small fraction of units returned to the factory. Of the 96 Torrent 9 units returned and stripped so far, all of which were logged as drain-pump claims, 31 had a faulty pump, 58 had an obstructed hose and 7 had neither.

**Source 3 — Claims and fleet data**

See the accompanying table. The two right-hand columns give the number of Torrent 9 units still under warranty and in customers' hands at the end of the month shown, split by build date.

accessibilityText: Three sources about warranty claims on a Torrent 9 dishwasher. Source 1, a service memo dated 6 May, reports 1,240 claims from January to April of which 812 cite the drain pump, says the drain-pump supplier changed from Velmark to Ostrey for every unit built on or after 1 December while earlier units carry a Velmark pump, says units reach customers on average two weeks after being built and carry a two-year warranty from that date, says the pump is the only component whose supplier changed, and proposes reverting to Velmark from 1 July. Source 2, an email from the supplier quality manager dated 11 May, gives two cautions: the same engineering release of 1 December also narrowed the drain hose from a 22 millimetre to a 19 millimetre internal bore, which raises the pressure the pump works against; and claim records classify a fault as drain pump whenever the machine fails to clear the sump, which a blocked or kinked hose also causes, with the component inspected only on units returned to the factory. Of 96 returned and stripped units, all logged as drain-pump claims, 31 had a faulty pump, 58 had an obstructed hose and 7 had neither. Source 3 is a four-row table by month. January: 214 claims, 102 citing the drain pump, 61 thousand in-warranty units built before 1 December, 9 thousand built on or after 1 December. February: 268 claims, 168 pump claims, 60 thousand and 18 thousand. March: 351 claims, 249 pump claims, 58 thousand and 29 thousand. April: 407 claims, 293 pump claims, 57 thousand and 41 thousand.

provenance.notes: Original multi-source set written for this question bank. The product, suppliers, dates and every figure are invented; nothing is drawn from any published Multi-Source Reasoning item. The monthly claim counts sum exactly to the totals quoted in Source 1 (1,240 and 812), and the strip-down counts sum to 96, so the three sources are numerically consistent and each question's data can be checked against more than one source.
